newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa faces ruling on route price.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa faces ruling on route price.

text.p: Germany's Federal Cartel Office said on Friday it would decide early in 1997 whether to issue airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG with an official warning over possibly inflated pricing on its Frankfurt-Berlin route.

The cartel authority has been investigating Lufthansa's pricing structures for nearly a year now, after complaints that its 860 mark business class fare on this route is some 150 marks more than the fare charged for a Munich-Berlin flight.
If the warning is issued, Lufthansa will be ordered to lower its Frankfurt-Berlin rate to bring it in line with its other fares, a spokeswoman for the cartel office said.
Lufthansa argues that the high Frankfurt-Berlin charge is necessary to cover the high costs which arise from unusually long waiting times at Frankfurt airport -- Germany's largest.
An airline spokeswoman said on Friday that Lufthansa had presented its case to the cartel authorities.
She said Lufthansa generally did not make enough on domestic flights to cover its costs, and that this was also the case with Frankfurt-Berlin.
